The Police Sub-Inspector of R.T. Nagara Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused No.1 for the offence punishable under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code by dropping out the accused No.2 to 4 namely Sri Doddaiah L @ Doddaiah L, Smt. Lakshmi @ Lashmi and Srividya @ Vidhya D.
2.
Prosecution Case:
The marriage of CW1 namely Smt. Vishrutha Srigandha was solemnized with accused No.1 on 20-05-2022 as per Hindu and customs.
After the marriage, the accused under influence of alcohol abused CW1 with filthy language and ill-treated her mentally and physically.
Unable to bear the harassment of accused, CW1 went to her parental house.
On 21-8-2022, the accused forcibly took CW1 from her parental house and beaten her whilst traveling in his car.
After sending CW1 to her parental house on 26-08-2022, he did not talk to her and did not take her to his house, thereby subjected her to mental and physical cruelty.
3. First Information Report:

Upon the receipt of first information, CW6/PW1 Sri Anil Kumar.T., the then PSI of R.T. Nagar Police Station registered Crime No.291/2022 against the accused No.1 to 4 for the offences punishable under Section 506, 498A KABC030133722023 CC No.7959/2023 of IPC and Sec.3, 4 of D.P. Act., prepared FIR as per Ex.P2 sent the same to the Court.
4.

Investigation: Thereafter on 01-02-2023 he drawn spot mahazar as per Ex.P3 from 11.30 am to 12.20 pm, secured the documents from CW1 as per Ex.P4 to Ex. P. 9, recorded the statement of witnesses and after completion of investigation, submitted charge sheet against the accused No.1 for the offence punishable under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code.

sentences.text: At pre-cognizance stage, the accused was enlarged on bail by the order dated 20-10-2022.
6. On receipt of charge sheet, this Court had taken cognizance for the offence alleged against the accused.
7. Copies of prosecution papers as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C have been furnished to the accused.
8. Charge:

After hearing learned Senior APP and counsel for accused, charge for offence punishable U/Sec 498A of Indian Penal Code has been framed, read over and explained to the accused persons in the language known to him, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
Prosecution Evidence:
The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 6 witnesses and examined 2 witnesses and exhibited 9 documents and closed their side.

Perused the nature of offence and PW2 being informant cum material witness did not support the prosecution case and hence the issuance of witness summons to other witnesses has been dispensed by the order dated 26/11/2025.

10. Accused statement as per section 313 of CrPC: After completion of evidence of prosecution, the accused examined as per section 313 of Cr.P.C wherein he denied all incriminating evidence appearing in the statement of prosecution witness and did not lead any rebuttal evidence.
11. Heard the arguments.
Perused materials on the record.

12. The following point are arises for consideration is as follows;
1. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that after the marriage of CW1 namely Smt. Vishrutha Srigandha with accused, the KABC030133722023 CC No.7959/2023 accused with influence of alcohol abused CW1 with filthy language, unable to bear the harassment of accused, CW1 went to her parental house.

On 21-8-2022, the accused forcibly took CW1 from her parental house and beaten her whilst traveling in his car and after sending CW1 to her parental house on 26-08-2022, he did not talk to her and did not take her to his house
thereby subjected her to mental and physical cruelty thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable under Sec.498(A) of IPC?
2. What order?

13. The findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 : In the Negative Point No.2 : As per final order KABC030133722023 CC No.7959/2023 REASONS R T Nagar Police Station vs Vikram D on 27 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44324493/

sentences.text: 14 . Point No.1: In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 12 of this judgment, the prosecution examined the following witnesses:

(i) CW6 by name Sri Anil Kumar.T., PSI of R.T.Nagara PS examined as PW1 and deposed that, on receipt of first information, he registered FIR as per Ex.P2, on 01-02-2023 he drawn spot mahazar as per Ex.P3 from 11.30 am to 12.20 pm, secured the documents from CW1 as per Ex.P4 to 9, recorded the statement of witnesses and after completion of investigation, submitted charge sheet against the accused No.1.

(ii) CW1 Smt. Vishrutha Srigandha, being informant examined as PW2 and identified her signatures on Ex.P1(complaint) and Ex.P3 (spot mahazar) as Ex.P1(b) and 3(b)
and deposed that when she went to the police station for sorting out the differences of opinion amongst her and the accused, the police obtained her signature on the said document.
Further deposed that she does not know the contents of Ex.P1 and Ex.P3 and she did not lodge any complaint against accused.

In this regard,

This court places reliance in the case of B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. State of haryana and anr in the case of AIR 2003 SCW 1824, wherein it was held that, "in a case where matrimonial disputes have been resolved between the parties then in that case offence under Section 498A of I.P.C. may be compounded between the parties for according to them an opportunity to settle in life afresh.

4 the case of Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat),
wherein this lordship observed which runs thus:
"It appears that good sense have been prevailed amongst the spouses and when it became impossible for them to lead conjugal life any further and when the matrimonial home has been broken for all practical purposes, they have decided to withdraw all allegations and counter allegations against each other and get themselves separated on divorce by mutual consent.

sentences.text: Although, Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code is not compoundable, but in the nature and circumstances of the case and the situation prevailing, accord is hereby granted to compromise the dispute KABC030133722023 CC No.7959/2023 between the parties and hence joint petition filed in both the cases are hereby allowed."

It further held that after examining the nature of the case and the circumstances, under which the offence has been committed, it would be proper to compound the offence and in my opinion, it would be also meet the ends of justice."
ADMITTEDLY, the disputes between the CW1 and accused have been resolved.
The criminal case under Section 498(A) of IPC are the off-shoot of the said matrimonial dispute.

16. In the case of the KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464,
wherein it was held that "it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end".

sentences.text: 17. Under these circumstances and on account of the preposition laid down by the Hon'ble Apex and Hon'ble High Court, even if other witnesses examined KABC030133722023 CC No.7959/2023 by the prosecution, they did supported the prosecution, would not helpful to the prosecution.
Under these circumstances, this court feels it is a waste of precious time of the Court in examining other witnesses.
Though the IO has examined as PW1, but his evidence is formal in nature and does not help to prosecution case.
Therefore, the prayer of learned Sr.APP is rejected and prosecution evidence is taken as closed and hence the ingredients for offence u/Section 498(A) of IPC was not proved beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, this court answer the point No.1 in the Negative.
18. Point No.2:-

In view of the above findings and reasons given on point No.1, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
(i) The accused No.1 is found not guilty and acquitted from the offence punishable under Sec.498(A) of Indian Penal Code.
(ii) Accused is set at liberty.
